resources.string: The fonts were applied after the boot, but the font service did not reload them. Open TypeFace Droplet to restart the system softly.
The fonts could not be applied after the boot: %1$s
The bundled fonts are inspected once after installation and after each update.
Replacing the system fonts changes system mounts, which only root can do. Set up one of the ways below.
Reading which fonts the system uses now.
The guard restored the original fonts
The system crashed while the replacement fonts were in use (%1$s), so the guard removed them at once. They are not applied at boot until you apply them again by hand.
After a restart of the device, %1$s applies them again while the system starts, before any application.
After a restart of the device, this application applies them again once the system has started.
They stay until the device restarts; applying at boot is turned off.
Choose fonts and apply them. Most applications switch to them at once, without a reboot.

Use su of Magisk, KernelSU or APatch (choose \"Grant\" when asked), Sui, or Shizuku started with root. Shizuku started through wireless debugging or ADB runs as the shell user, which cannot change system mounts.
%1$d font families were replaced. Applications started from now on use the new fonts.
%1$d font families were replaced. The system interface, the home screen and the applications in the background were restarted, so that they use the new fonts too.

The fonts are in place, but the font service of this system cannot reload them by itself (it can only with fs-verity). A soft restart restarts the system services and every application, without rebooting the device.
No rule matched any font family of this system. Choose fonts, or check the rules.
The fonts are applied, but applying them at boot could not be set up: %1$s
They also stay after a restart of the device. Applications that are running keep the replacement fonts until they restart.
The system services restart now; the screen goes dark for a moment.

su runs this application as root, but the root manager has removed the capabilities of root, so fonts can be neither applied nor restored. In Magisk, open Superuser and change the access of TypeFace Droplet from \"Restrict\" to \"Grant\". Other root managers have similar settings, such as the app profile of KernelSU.
The quick brown fox · 永字八法
No way to run as root yet
Applied by %1$s while the system starts
No root manager runs boot scripts; this application applies them after the boot
Applied by this application after the boot
Watching the system after the change; it restores the original fonts if the system crashes.
%1$d disabled while the fonts are applied
Runs through ADB as the shell user, which cannot change system mounts. Start Shizuku with root, or use Sui or su.
This application has not been granted access yet.
The installed version is too old.
Choose a font for each kind of text. Families of the system that use these kinds, such as Roboto and Google Sans, follow your choice.
The library is empty. Import a TTF, OTF or TTC file.
The text of almost every application and of the system.
Text that asks for a serif typeface, such as articles and books.
Code, terminals and other text that aligns characters in columns.
The upright font, slanted by the system
Keep the font of the system for this kind of text.
The system slants the upright font.
%1$d faces; the first one is used
Family name written into the font

Applications that look fonts up by name (such as Firefox) find the font under this name. Left empty, the font is installed once for each family it replaces and takes the name of its original fonts (such as Roboto, Google Sans and Noto Serif).
The font file is deleted from the library.
Fonts in use cannot be removed.
Roles and rules are edited by hand
Choosing fonts changes only the faces of the roles sans, serif and mono. Reset to make the roles and rules follow the chosen fonts again.
Choosing fonts changes the faces of the roles sans, serif and mono that your rules use.
The recommended rules are in use
They follow the fonts you choose. Editing a role or a rule switches to rules edited by hand.
Fonts, roles, rules, components and restart targets return to the recommended configuration with the bundled fonts. Imported fonts stay in the library.
No roles. A role is a set of fonts that replaces system font families.
Values for variation axes other than wght and ital (for example opsz or GRAD), for every face of the role.
The role and every rule that uses it are deleted.
Optional. Overrides the weight of a static font, or pins the wght axis of a variable font.
Fixed axes of this face (override those of the role)
Rules decide which system font families each role replaces. They are tried from the top; the first rule that matches a family decides.
A family name, such as sans-serif. * matches anything and ? matches one character.
A font file name without extension, such as Roboto-*. Named families that use a matching file are replaced.
A BCP 47 language tag, such as ja, matched against the first language of fallback families.
A fallback family made of these roles is inserted before the first matching fallback family. Fallback-for names the generic family (serif, monospace) a font serves.
The named font families of this system. Tap one to assign a role or a font to it.
Reading the families of the system needs root.
Choose a role, or a single font. A rule for exactly this family is added first, so it overrides the other rules.
Automatic uses Sui or Shizuku when it runs as root, and su otherwise.
The root manager applies the fonts at every boot, before the system starts any application. No restart and no soft restart is needed.
No root manager that runs boot scripts (Magisk, KernelSU, APatch) was found.
%1$s will apply them while the system starts, once the fonts are applied.
When the fonts are not active after a boot, this application applies them once the system has started.
Restart the applications in the background

Running applications keep the fonts they started with. These are restarted after applying and restoring, so that they show the change at once. Background applications are only those the system may close safely.
Disable downloadable fonts of Google Play services
Applications that download fonts such as Google Sans from Google Play services then use the system fonts.
Components are disabled for every user while the fonts are applied, and restored when the original fonts are restored.

After a change, the guard watches the system for this long. If the system crashes, it restores the original fonts at once, and the fonts are not applied at boot until you apply them by hand. At boot it always watches until the system has started, and then at least 30 seconds.
Generate font configurations even when their version is newer than this version knows.
The engine keeps installed fonts and the configuration applied at boot in %1$s.
Nercone Sans, Serif and Mono CJK NF, licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

When TypeFace Droplet is uninstalled while it applies fonts at boot through a root manager, the next boot uses the original fonts, and once the system has started, the engine re-enables the components it disabled and removes its files. Otherwise, restore the original fonts before uninstalling, so that the components are enabled again.
